title: Prompting vs RAG vs Fine Tuning

scenes.text: You want an AI that knows your business. [1] Should you write a better prompt, use RAG, or fine tune a model? [2] Let's settle it.

First, what is fine tuning? [1] It means training an existing model a little more, on your own examples, so it learns a new style or skill. [2] It needs lots of examples. [3] It changes how the model behaves. [4] And it costs time and money.

data.definition: Extra training on your own examples, so the model learns a style or skill.

scenes.text: Think of a new employee. [1] Prompting is giving clear instructions for today's task. [2] RAG is handing them the company handbook, to look things up. [3] Fine tuning is sending them on a months long training course.

data.heading: Think: a new employee
items: Send them on a training course

scenes.text: Here's the cheat sheet. [1] Three options. [2] Setup cost. Prompting is basically free. RAG is low. Fine tuning is high. [3] Fresh or private information? RAG wins. [4] A special style or format? Fine tuning wins. [5] Speed to get started? Prompting, in minutes. [6] Rule of thumb. Start with prompts, add RAG for knowledge, fine tune for behaviour.

data.heading: The cheat sheet
data.note: Prompt first → RAG for knowledge → fine-tune for behaviour

scenes.text: Real examples. [1] A startup writing social media captions. Good prompts are enough. [2] A law firm answering from thousands of case files. RAG. [3] A telecom company that wants replies in its exact brand tone, every single time. Fine tuning.

Here's a common myth. [1] Fine tuning is the best way to teach a model new facts. [2] Usually not. Fine tuning is great for style and behaviour. For facts that change, RAG is cheaper, and easier to update.

data.myth: Fine-tuning is the best way to add new facts.
data.fact: Fine-tuning shapes style and behaviour. For changing facts, RAG is cheaper and easier to update.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! Your prices change every week, and the chatbot must always know the latest. Which one? [1] Pause and think. <pause 3.2> [2] RAG! Update the documents, and answers update instantly. Comment RAG!

Recap. [1] Prompting is instructions. Always start there. [2] RAG adds knowledge that stays fresh. [3] Fine tuning teaches style and behaviour. [4] And real apps often combine all three. [5] Next episode, tool use. How AI can check the weather, book a cab, or send an email. Follow AI Maastaaru!
